principles: Use existing ProofStory ledger facts as the source of truth.
Keep milestone_status read-only and fail closed on mutation-like flags.
Show complete/current/remaining progress in one stable table after each material status change.
Expose missing evidence or missing ledger detail explicitly instead of inventing completion state.
drivers: The user needs visible milestone progress with sub-objective detail.
The existing ProofStory contract says milestone ledgers are intent coverage, not a second execution machine.
Lifecycle gates must remain owned by existing validate/review/DONE handlers.

options.name: Read-only projection over existing ProofStory ledger
pros: Reuses existing milestone-ledger storage and checklist/evidence facts.
Lowest risk because it does not advance phases or write evidence.
Gives hosts a stable table immediately while preserving future writer integration.
cons: Transition details are limited until future completion-writer or executor-ledger artifacts exist.

options.name: New milestone execution ledger
pros: Could store rich sub-objective transition history immediately.
cons: Creates a second source of truth and conflicts with the ProofStory contract.
Higher risk of hosts treating report rows as lifecycle authority.

options.name: Full automatic lifecycle pipeline
pros: Could eventually reduce host manual steps across execution, validation, review, and DONE.
cons: Too broad for V1 and risks duplicating lifecycle gates, reviewer lanes, and evidence writers.

chosen: Read-only projection over existing ProofStory ledger
rationale: Choose a read-only projection because the immediate problem is progress visibility, not new execution authority. This preserves existing ProofStory ledger semantics and makes later completion-writer integration additive rather than a competing truth source.

preMortem.scenario: milestone_status is mistaken for a command that marks milestones done
preMortem.trigger: The text renderer uses DONE-like wording without explaining read-only status.
preMortem.consequence: Hosts may overclaim progress and bypass evidence gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Renderer includes read-only/no mutation language and next action rows instead of mutating state.

preMortem.scenario: The implementation creates a parallel milestone schema
preMortem.trigger: Sub-objective detail is stored outside the existing ProofStory ledger/checklist/evidence facts.
preMortem.consequence: Milestone facts drift and reviewers cannot tell which source is authoritative.
preMortem.mitigation: V1 only projects existing ledger/checklist/evidence facts and treats richer completion writer artifacts as future extension.

preMortem.scenario: Missing or stale evidence is shown as complete
preMortem.trigger: Classifier trusts checklist or ledger status without checking verificationEvidence presence.
preMortem.consequence: The report becomes a false-DONE surface.
preMortem.mitigation: Rows with done-like ledger status but missing evidence get warnings/next actions and are not silently treated as complete.
